proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an exact common-flow compression-loss identity, complementary-path witnesses with unbounded loss, a count-conditional hybrid confidence construction, dominant-skeleton efficiency, and a rich-support full-law score-range result; it also delivered a tested comparator prototype and verified the Pinelis citation. D0.5 nevertheless capped the package at subfield because the strongest efficiency and converse claims cover restricted law classes and the feasible procedure requires known design structure. Four panel findings remain unrepaired because novelty triage stopped before a soundness-repair round; any re-raised program must resolve those findings and materially broaden the scope rather than merely polish the existing note.
tldr: The paper separates the two group-edge mean systems in a fixed finite rotating panel. It proves separate-graph identification, the sum of treated and comparison effective resistances as the regular mean-model information bound, an exact common-flow compression loss, and complementary-path families with unbounded loss inside the no-covariate Bell'ego full-distribution Missing Trends At Random subclass. Its count-conditional hybrid confidence set is honest with finite cells and attains the oracle two-resistance length whenever a fixed connecting skeleton has merely diverging minimum expected count, square-root maximum count negligible relative to that minimum, and negligible deleted-edge information. This includes balanced skeleton counts growing as slowly as \(\log n\) or \(\log\log n\). For full-law efficiency, the observed score map is explicit: the bound equals the two-resistance benchmark exactly when the electrical mean-model gradient belongs to the closure of the compatible full-trajectory score range, and equality is proved for simple chronological graphs with rich convex cut-space support.
gap: Published chained DiD transports each group's changes but its general-missingness workflow stacks already differenced ATT increments. Existing network-flow theory already owns two-graph connectivity and resistance ideas in an additive unit-time model, yet no located result gives the exact common-flow projection loss for the rotating-panel mean-transport experiment or joins it to honest inference when essential cells have finite expected counts.
fill: The proposed paper will specialize the established connectivity and two-resistance results to a causally explicit observed-mark experiment, then contribute the squared-flow loss identity, a faithful common-moment comparator, an unbounded fixed-count complementary-path family, a fully specified conditional confidence algorithm, dense oracle equivalence for the known fixed-graph two-rate design, and a bounded Hellinger lower bound. It will explicitly leave full-distribution tangent-space equality, unknown assignment probabilities, and intermediate-rate adaptation open.
